scope: warehouse.command_document creation and transition COMMIT recovery
database: PostgreSQL 17, disposable cluster bound to 127.0.0.1 and a dynamically allocated port, prepared with scripts/prepare-test-db.py

red.observed: A real pgx socket's COMMIT Write returned a generic transport error before sending the commit. HTTP 500 internal_error was returned, without the same-command retry contract. An independent admin connection confirmed zero committed operation receipts.
red.expected: HTTP 503 operation_interrupted with Retry-After and instruction to retry the same command identifier
already_passing_characterization: Server committed and its acknowledgement was discarded as EOF (both commands)
Server committed and its acknowledgement was discarded as a generic read error (both commands)
Deferred PostgreSQL constraint rejection at COMMIT remains a definitive HTTP 409 rollback (both commands)

implementation.change: Translate explicit PostgreSQL COMMIT errors normally; classify every other COMMIT failure as an unconfirmed operation and require recovery with the original command ID. Matches the existing inventory command contract.

asserted_invariants: Before-send transport loss rolls back documents and operation receipts
Lost acknowledgement occurs after the server durably commits, independently observed through an admin connection
Recovery returns exactly the durable original response on repeated retries
Create/transition modifies document state, version and content_revision exactly once
Recovery leaves exactly one operation, audit entry and outbox event and does not change inventory
Explicit deferred PostgreSQL constraint rejection is not hidden as transport uncertainty
Generated kinds, line counts and decimal quantities preserve document lines and quantities
Mismatched optimistic versions reject without operation receipts or state changes
Incomplete documents cannot close and cancelled documents cannot reactivate
Replaying creation after later transitions returns its original snapshot
Reusing a successful command ID with changed input rejects
Invalid precision after a generated valid prefix rolls back the entire create and leaves its command ID reusable
honesty_notes: Initial test harness errors (uppercase matching while pgx sends lowercase commit, and expecting version conflict instead of input validation for version zero) were corrected before the recorded final RED run; neither was attributed to production code.
Property checks characterized existing correct behavior and are not presented as red-to-green production fixes.
This local evidence does not substitute for successful CI on the final pushed revision.
